abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a prevalent psychiatric condition with substantial personal and societal impact, yet its identification in large-scale populations still relies primarily on symptom-based clinical assessment. We introduce MD 3 S ( M ajor D epressive D isorder D etection S ystem), an artificial intelligence-assisted screening framework for identifying individuals with documented MDD using routinely collected laboratory and clinical information. Leveraging over 180,000 real-world health assessment records from the UK Biobank, MD 3 S integrates hematological, biochemical, and physiological indicators to distinguish individuals with MDD from non-MDD controls in a retrospective multicenter setting. To evaluate cross-population generalizability, we further validated the framework in two independent external hospital-based cohorts. MD 3 S achieved an accuracy of 86.57% on the internal validation dataset and maintained robust performance across two independent external validation cohorts. Compared with conventional machine learning and deep learning approaches, MD 3 S demonstrates improved predictive performance, stable cross-cohort transferability, and high computational efficiency. These findings highlight that routine laboratory data may support scalable AI-assisted screening strategies for identifying individuals with MDD across diverse clinical and population settings.

title: Artificial intelligence-assisted screening of major depressive disorder using routine laboratory tests across multicenter cohorts
